title: Honey and Oat Flapjacks
subtitle: Chewy golden oat bars
excerpt: Rolled oats bound with butter, honey, and flaked almonds, pressed into a tin and baked until golden. They are crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle.
sourceNotes: Based on the classic British flapjack, using honey in place of golden syrup and topped with flaked almonds.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooled bars in a single layer, then transfer to a bag. Eat within 2 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 5 days.

content.text: Press the mixture firmly into the tin before baking. This is what gives flapjacks their chewy, compact texture rather than a crumbly one.
Heat the oven to 160C (140C fan). Grease and line a 20x30cm baking tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter and honey together in a large saucepan over low heat. Stir until combined.
Remove from the heat. Add the oats and flaked almonds. Stir until every oat is coated.
Tip the mixture into the prepared tin. Press down very firmly with the back of a spoon.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden at the edges. The centre will look slightly underdone.
Leave to cool in the tin for 10 minutes. Mark into 16 bars while still warm.
Leave to cool completely in the tin, then chill for 30 minutes before cutting through the marks.

items.cause: Not pressed firmly enough or cut while still warm.
items.fix: Press harder next time and chill for 30 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: Flapjacks are too hard and dry.
items.fix: Reduce baking time by 5 minutes and check earlier next time.

items.cause: Honey burned onto the tin surface.
items.fix: Use baking paper and leave to cool 10 minutes before removing.
